lesson.child_mission: Climate affects how people live, including their homes, clothing, food, work, transport and recreation. People adapt to the climate using local materials and knowledge, though cost, culture and technology also matter.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Link climate to a feature: heavy snow; a hot dry desert; a cyclone-prone coast. Write one home or clothing feature for each.

FEEDBACK
Snow: steep roof and warm layers; hot desert: thick walls, shade and light clothing; cyclone coast: strong roof fixings and shutters.

WATCH FOR
Saying climate is the only reason people live the way they do ignores cost, culture and technology.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Choose two very different climates. Make a cause and effect table showing how climate affects homes, clothing and food or work. Use at least two sources.

Write a short reflection naming one source or idea you corrected and why.

lesson.parent_notes:
Parent: Marking guidance for the independent task: Choose two very different climates. Make a cause and effect table showing how climate affects homes, clothing and food or work. Use at least two sources. Accept equivalent original responses that show the same skill.

Parent: Written model 1: Original demonstration: Example: in the hot, wet tropics homes may be built on stilts for airflow and flooding, with wide verandahs for shade. In regions that face cyclones, building rules require strong roofs and fixings. People wear light clothes in the heat and waterproof clothing in heavy rain.

Parent: Written model 2: Common error: Saying climate is the only reason people live the way they do ignores cost, culture and technology. Correction: Snow: steep roof and warm layers; hot desert: thick walls, shade and light clothing; cyclone coast: strong roof fixings and shutters.

Parent: Likely misconception: Saying climate is the only reason people live the way they do ignores cost, culture and technology. Keep sample answers out of the child role.
